question: What was Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier's most important contribution to chemistry in 1789?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Conservation of Mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Law of Conservation of Mass was formulated by Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier in 1789.
 
• This law states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• Lavoisier's work helped to transform chemistry from a qualitative to a quantitative science.
 
• He demonstrated that the total mass of reactants in a chemical reaction is equal to the total mass of products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• This law is fundamental to the study of chemistry and physics.
 
• It implies that in a closed system, the mass of the system remains constant over time.
 
• Lavoisier's experiments involved careful measurements and the use of a balance to weigh reactants and products.
 
• He showed that combustion and respiration are processes that involve the combination of substances with oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:**
 
 
• Formulated by John Dalton in the early 19th century.
 
• This law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
 
 
• **Law of Definite Proportions:**
 
 
• Also known as Proust's Law, formulated by Joseph Proust.
 
• This law states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratio by mass, and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• States that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time.
 
• Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but can only be transformed from one form to another.
